scenes.heading: Your repo, explained in one command.
scenes.sub: A narrated video, a better README and a launch kit, from any repository.
scenes.say: Most repositories never get understood. A visitor gives the README a few seconds, sees a wall of text, and leaves. reporeel fixes that with one command.
First it scores the repo the way a visitor sees it. This little app gets a D: no demo, no license, no way to know what it does.
Then run reporeel with no arguments. It writes a storyboard, records a narrated video, draws the architecture, makes a social card and updates the README. The score goes up on its own.

type: Paste any text. See how long it takes to read, and how hard it is. Short sentences help.

scenes.say: Web scenes drive the real app, with a cursor that glides, clicks that ripple, and a camera that zooms in on what matters.

scenes.caption: the whole contract
scenes.say: Everything lives in one storyboard file. Title cards, live web, real code, diagrams, terminal runs and numbers. A coding agent writes it, or Claude does, or you do.

scenes.caption: How it works
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  R[Your repo] --> P[plan: agent or Claude]
  P --> S[reporeel.json]
  S --> V[voice: Kokoro or ElevenLabs]
  S --> B[Chrome screencast]
  V --> F[ffmpeg]
  B --> F
  F --> O[MP4, GIF, captions]
  O --> D[README, social card, launch posts]
scenes.say: The narration is spoken by a free local voice, or by ElevenLabs in Hindi and many other languages. Chrome records sharp frames, and ffmpeg puts it all together.
